thread:
oliver: Quick thought — we should add a lightweight escape hatch for the continuous batcher when tail latency or KV-cache miss storms occur. Current fallback to full microbatching is too blunt and increases cost a lot.

anya: +1. What are you picturing as an escape hatch? a config flag, runtime signal, or an operator-driven switch? :thinking:

oliver: Prefer automatic signal-based with an operator override. Something like a two-tiered degrade path: 1) soft mode where we reduce coalesce window and prefetch aggressively, 2) hard mode where we redirect small requests to a tiny-window microfastpath.

kevin: I worry about coupling the scheduler to metrics. We need a clean interface so the admission layer just receives a "mode" enum and deadlines, not internal signals. That keeps boundaries for Private/Dedicated deployments.

maria: Agreed. Proposed interface: scheduler.admit(request, hints) -> {action: keep|route-microfast|route-fallback, reason: string}. Hints can include soft_deadline_ms and kv_cache_hit_rate. Keep the heuristics inside runtime but expose minimal contract.

oliver: Exactly. The heuristics module can subscribe to observability streams (p90 latency, inflight batches, kv miss rate) and flip the mode. We should also emit a short audit event so Console can show when escape hatch triggered.

kevin: For implementation: add a tiny state machine in the coalescer with explicit transitions: NORMAL -> SOFT_DEGRADE -> HARD_DEGRADE -> RECOVERING. Each transition has backoff and hysteresis. Avoid flapping.

anya: What about tenant fairness? If we flip globally, noisy tenants still dominate. We should allow per-tenant soft_deadline adjustments and a global circuit breaker.

maria: Per-tenant param makes sense. Default behavior: try per-tenant soft_degrade first; if >X% tenants degraded or cluster p90 crosses threshold, flip global.

oliver: Implementation sketch (pseudo-config):
```
batcher.escape_hatch.enabled = true
batcher.escape_hatch.soft_deadline_ms = 40
batcher.escape_hatch.hard_deadline_ms = 15
batcher.escape_hatch.per_tenant_threshold = 0.2
```

kevin: Also add observability hooks: emit metrics for transition count, degraded_tenants, and average per-tenant batch size. That will help Optimize recommend quantization/batching changes later.

maria: One more thing — keep the admission API backwards compatible. New "hints" param optional. Default server behavior equals current. We can ship heuristics behind a feature flag.

ci-bot: deploybot: rolling rollout to canary cluster queued (canary: batcher-escape-hatch-v0.1). Logs will show transition events under /observability/escape_hatch.

anya: Next steps: 1) Kevin to draft the admit() contract PR, 2) Oliver to prototype the state machine in the coalescer, 3) Maria to add Console/event hooks. We'll iterate on thresholds after canary telemetry.

oliver: Thanks — I'll open the PR with a minimal implementation and a test harness that simulates kv-miss storms.

kevin: If anyone wants to discuss corner cases (e.g., long-running streaming requests), ping me offline.

maria: Adding a checklist to the PR for backwards compatibility and docs.

oliver: Cool. That should give us a less risky, more surgical escape hatch than full microbatch fallback. :thumbsup:
